name: JustThirty
subtitle: A clear limit for distractions
promotionalText: One combined 30-minute daily window for distracting apps and websites. Start, pause, and resume. Free, private, and built for your iPhone.
description:
A little access. A clear stopping point.

JustThirty helps you put distance between yourself and distracting apps and websites. Choose what you want to limit, then give everything on your list one combined 30-minute daily allowance on your iPhone.

START. PAUSE. RESUME.
Start access when you want to open your selected apps and sites. Pause to block them again and save your unused time. Resume later that day. The timer keeps running while you switch away or lock your phone, so pause when you're done. When the allowance ends, blocking returns.

ADD WITH INTENTION
Choose apps and categories with Apple's Screen Time picker. Search familiar websites or paste a domain. Review every addition carefully: entries cannot be removed inside JustThirty. There is no extra-time purchase or in-app reset.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
Your block list and timer stay on your device. No account, analytics, advertising, or cloud sync. Website suggestions are searched locally.

CLEAR LIMITS
JustThirty uses Apple's Screen Time tools. Website coverage depends on the browser. iOS still lets you revoke Screen Time access or delete the app. Adding typed website restrictions also disables Safari Private Browsing. JustThirty is a personal commitment tool; it cannot make your device impossible to override.

The daily allowance resets at midnight in the original allowance time zone. Unused minutes do not carry over. Each device has its own allowance.

Free and open source. Requires iOS 17.4 or later.
reviewNotes:
JustThirty is a free individual focus and productivity app. No app account or sign-in is required. It uses AuthorizationCenter.requestAuthorization(for: .individual), FamilyActivityPicker, ManagedSettings, and a DeviceActivityMonitor extension. It is not intended to manage another adult's device or serve advertising.

Review flow:
1. On a physical iPhone, enable Screen Time access in the app.
2. Add a disposable test app or website. Review the permanent-add confirmation. There is no in-app removal/reset; use a test device because entries are add-only.
3. With access paused, verify the selected target is shielded.
4. Tap Start access, then Start. All saved entries share one combined 30-minute wall-clock allowance on this device.
5. Tap Pause access: restrictions return and unused time is preserved. Resume access uses the remaining allowance. The timer runs in the background and while locked. The monitor extension restores restrictions at the scheduled end.
6. The allowance resets at midnight in the time zone where it was initially created. Devices have independent allowances.

No usage reports or browsing history are uploaded. Typed domain suggestions are local. Apple controls authorization and browser coverage. The in-app explanation discloses that iOS authorization revocation or deletion can bypass restrictions, and typed-domain filtering disables Safari Private Browsing.

The existing bundle IDs are retained from the app's original OneWay name to preserve users' local data. The display name is JustThirty. The logo is unchanged.
